arxiv-2002-06701.title: Gaussian Smoothen Semantic Features (GSSF) - Exploring the Linguistic Aspects of Visual Captioning in Indian Languages (Bengali) Using MSCOCO Framework
arxiv-2002-06701.creator: Chiranjib Sur
arxiv-2002-06701.description: Abstract In this work, we have introduced Gaussian Smoothen Semantic Features (GSSF) for Better Semantic Selection for Indian regional language-based image captioning and introduced a procedure where we used the existing translation and English crowd-sourced sentences for training. We have shown that this architecture is a promising alternative source, where there is a crunch in resources.

arxiv-2206-06185.title: T c ​ c + ​ ( 3875 ) T_{cc}^{+}(3875) relevant D ​ D ∗ DD^{*} scattering from N f = 2 N_{f}=2 lattice QCD
arxiv-2206-06185.creator: Siyang Chen, Chunjiang Shi, Ying Chen, Ming Gong, Zhaofeng Liu, Wei Sun, Renqiang Zhang
arxiv-2206-06185.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Siyang Chen, Chunjiang Shi, Ying Chen, Ming Gong, Zhaofeng Liu, Wei Sun, Renqiang Zhang. The S S -wave D ​ D ∗ DD^{*} scattering in the isospin I = 0 , 1 I=0,1 channels is studied in N f = 2 N_{f}=2 lattice QCD at m π ≈ 350 m_{\pi}\approx 350 MeV.

arxiv-2305-06675.title: Rokhlin Dimension: Permanence Properties and Ideal Separation
arxiv-2305-06675.creator: Sureshkumar M, Prahlad Vaidyanathan
arxiv-2305-06675.description: Abstract . We study the Rokhlin dimension for actions of residually finite groups on C*-algebras. We give a definition equivalent to the original one due to Szabó, Wu and Zacharias. We then prove a number of permanence properties and discuss actions on C 0 ​ ( X ) C_{0}(X) -algebras and commutative C*-algebras.

arxiv-2311-18635.title: DiffusionAvatars: Deferred Diffusion for High-fidelity 3D Head Avatars
arxiv-2311-18635.creator: Tobias Kirschstein, Simon Giebenhain, Matthias Nießner
arxiv-2311-18635.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Tobias Kirschstein, Simon Giebenhain, Matthias Nießner. DiffusionAvatars synthesizes a high-fidelity 3D head avatar of a person, offering intuitive control over both pose and expression. We propose a diffusion-based neural renderer that leverages generic 2D priors to produce compelling images of faces. For coarse guidance of the expression and head pose, we render a neural parametric head model (NPHM) from the target viewpoint, which acts as a proxy geometry of the person.

arxiv-2402-17615.title: A Multi-Agent Model for Opinion Evolution under Cognitive Biases
arxiv-2402-17615.creator: Mário S. Alvim, Artur Gaspar da Silva, Sophia Knight, Frank Valencia
arxiv-2402-17615.description: Abstract We generalize the DeGroot model for opinion dynamics to better capture realistic social scenarios. We introduce a model where each agent has their own individual cognitive biases . Society is represented as a directed graph whose edges indicate how much agents influence one another.

arxiv-2504-01750.title: Probing the Distance Duality Relation with Machine Learning and Recent Data
arxiv-2504-01750.creator: Alain Blanchard
arxiv-2504-01750.description: Abstract The distance duality relation (DDR) relates two independent ways of measuring cosmological distances, namely the angular diameter distance and the luminosity distance. These can be measured with baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) and Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia), respectively. Here, we use recent DESI DR1, Pantheon+, SH0ES and DES-SN5YR data to test this fundamental relation.

arxiv-2504-19812.title: Hyper-differential sensitivity analysis with respect to model discrepancy: Prior Distributions
arxiv-2504-19812.creator: Bart van Bloemen Waanders, Jixian Li, Timbwaoga A. J. Ouermi, Chris R. Johnson
arxiv-2504-19812.description: Abstract Hyper-differential sensitivity analysis with respect to model discrepancy was recently developed to enable uncertainty quantification for optimization problems. The approach consists of two primary steps: (i) Bayesian calibration of the discrepancy between high- and low-fidelity models, and (ii) propagating the model discrepancy uncertainty through the optimization problem.

arxiv-2507-11921.title: Spin-Valley Locking and Pure Spin-Triplet Superconductivity in Noncollinear Antiferromagnets Proximitized to Conventional Superconductors
arxiv-2507-11921.creator: Song-Bo Zhang, Lun-Hui Hu, Qian Niu, Zhenyu Zhang
arxiv-2507-11921.description: Abstract Unconventional antiferromagnets with spin-split bands, such as noncollinear magnets and the recently discovered altermagnets, serve as new constituents to explore unconventional superconductivity. Here, we unveil a new type and previously unappreciated nature of spin-valley locking in noncollinear antiferromagnets and exploit this texture to achieve pure spin-triplet superconductivity. pmc-10621108.title: Predicting active enhancers with DNA methylation and histone modification
pmc-10621108.creator: Ximei Luo, Qun Li, Yifan Tang, Yan Liu, Quan Zou, Jie Zheng, Ying Zhang, Lei Xu
pmc-10621108.description: BackgroundEnhancers play a crucial role in gene regulation, and some active enhancers produce noncoding RNAs known as enhancer RNAs (eRNAs) bi-directionally. The most commonly used method for detecting eRNAs is CAGE-seq, but the instability of eRNAs in vivo leads to data noise in sequencing results.

pmc-10738596.title: FROM THE WORKROOM TO THE BEDROOM: MEDIATING EFFECTS OF WORK-TO-FAMILY SPILLOVER ON WORK CHARACTERISTICS AND SLEEP
pmc-10738596.creator: Kian Huang, Christina Mu, Claire Smith, Soomi Lee
pmc-10738596.description: Negative and positive work experiences may spillover to the home domain and harm one’s sleep. This study investigated whether work-to-family spillover mediates the relationship between work characteristics and sleep health. Full-time workers (n=2,106) from the Midlife in the United States Study provided Time-1 data (T1: 2004-2006); a sub-set (n=1,444) was reassessed at Time-2 (T2: 2013-2015).

pmc-10781615.title: Osteochondroma of the Mandibular Condyle: A Rare Case Presentation With Literature Review
pmc-10781615.creator: Dilasha Dhungel, Varun Rastogi, Nisha Maddheshiya, Sandhya Chaurasia, Karthikeyan Ramalingam
pmc-10781615.description: Osteochondromas (OCs) are benign bone tumors characterized by their growth with a cartilage cap and typically occurring at the ends of long bones. Their occurrence in the head and neck region is infrequent, accounting for only around 1% of head and neck tumors.

pmc-11319354.title: Allopolyploidization from two dioecious ancestors leads to recurrent evolution of sex chromosomes
pmc-11319354.creator: Li He, Yuàn Wang, Yi Wang, Ren-Gang Zhang, Yuán Wang, Elvira Hörandl, Tao Ma, Yan-Fei Mao, Judith E Mank, Ray Ming
pmc-11319354.description: Polyploidization presents an unusual challenge for species with sex chromosomes, as it can lead to complex combinations of sex chromosomes that disrupt reproductive development. This is particularly true for allopolyploidization between species with different sex chromosome systems. Here, we assemble haplotype-resolved chromosome-level genomes of a female allotetraploid weeping willow (Salix babylonica) and a male diploid S. dunnii.

pmc-11607794.title: Effect of WhatsApp Messenger-based education on the knowledge of health ambassadors about home care for minor illnesses
pmc-11607794.creator: Fatemeh Abbasian, Mohammad Mehdi Naghizadeh, Leila Ahmadian
pmc-11607794.description: BackgroundIn the digital era, virtual education has become one of the most effective educational methods, in which, the latest educational materials can be made available to people using social network platforms. Health ambassadors are mediators for transferring health-related knowledge to the public, so, they must be aware of various health topics, such as home care for minor illnesses.

pmc-12504726.title: A dual-branch pedestrian re-identification method CPHMNet based on multi-dimensional feature fusion and integrated pose estimation
pmc-12504726.creator: Huizhi Xu, Ruijie Gao
pmc-12504726.description: To address the interferences in pedestrian feature extraction caused by pose variations and occlusions, which adversely affect recognition performance in pedestrian re-identification tasks, this paper proposes a pedestrian re-identification method, CPHMNet, based on multi-dimensional feature fusion and integrated pose estimation. Firstly, a novel MDA module is developed to enhance the capability of feature discrimination for similar pedestrians.

pmc-12630272.title: Delaunay-Like Compact Equilibria in the Liquid Drop Model
pmc-12630272.creator: Manuel del Pino, Monica Musso, Andres Zuniga
pmc-12630272.description: The liquid drop model was introduced by Gamow in 1928 and Bohr–Wheeler in 1938 to model atomic nuclei. The model describes the competition between the surface tension, which keeps the nuclei together, and the Coulomb force, corresponding to repulsion among protons.

pmc-12653910.title: Beyond Thrombopoiesis: The Immune Functions of Megakaryocytes in Bacterial Infections and Sepsis
pmc-12653910.creator: Marina Leardini-Tristão, Meenakshi Banerjee, Pablo C Baldi
pmc-12653910.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Megakaryocytes (MKs) are specialized hematopoietic cells long recognized for their ability to produce platelets. Increasing evidence now highlights MKs as multifunctional immune effectors that bridge hematopoiesis with host immunity. In the bone marrow (BM), MKs arise through thrombopoietin (TPO)-mediated differentiation of hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) and show substantial heterogeneity, with discrete subsets specialized for platelet production (thrombopoiesis), HSC niche maintenance, or immune modulation.

pmc-12730767.title: Temporal trends in the causes of in-hospital cardiac arrest: a retrospective observational cohort study on the limitations of the current alert system at a tertiary hospital in Korea
pmc-12730767.creator: Joong Min Lee, Min Soo Cho, Myung-Jin Cha, Jun Kim, Kee-Joon Choi, Ah-Ram Kim, Min-Seok Kim, JinMi Lee, Yujung Shin, Un Jung Go, Hae Yeon Oh, Sang-Bum Hong, Gi-Byoung Nam
pmc-12730767.description: ObjectivesIn-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) is associated with high mortality and serious neurological sequelae. Although medical alert systems have evolved, the ability of these systems to influence changes in IHCA incidence and aetiology remains limited.DesignsRetrospective observational cohort study.SettingsA single tertiary hospital in South Korea, covering tertiary care levels.

pmc-13113428.title: Antibiotic Resistance and Genomic Diversity of Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Clonal Complex 45 Isolates in Kuwait Hospitals
pmc-13113428.creator: Samar S. Boswihi, Tina Verghese, Edet E. Udo
pmc-13113428.description: Background/Objectives: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) causes hospital- and community-acquired infections. MRSA is a highly diverse strain that includes several epidemic clones, including CC45. A previous study conducted among MRSA isolates in Kuwait identified CC45 in two isolates in the early 2000s.

pmc-13137804.title: Development and Structural Characterization of UTE‐156, a Covalent Inhibitor of the VCP/p97 AAA+ ATPase
pmc-13137804.creator: Daniela Tamayo‐Jaramillo, Subramanya Hegde, Xuan Jia, Kimberly Coffman, Hariprasad Vankayalapati, David Bearss, Kevin B Jones, Alex W Stark, Peter S Shen
pmc-13137804.description: The AAA+ ATPase valosin‐containing protein (VCP/p97) is a central regulator of protein homeostasis that is well characterized for its role in extracting and remodeling ubiquitinated substrates. Dysregulation of VCP activity contributes to the pathogenesis of neurodegenerative diseases and cancer, making it an important therapeutic target.

pmc-13206654.title: Tracheotomy Before Total Laryngectomy as a Risk Factor for Stoma Recurrence
pmc-13206654.creator: Andreza de Jesus Prates, Otávio Alberto Curioni, Daniel Marin Ramos, Bruno Pelinson Fogaça Duarte, Rogério Aparecido Dedivitis
pmc-13206654.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background/Objectives: Laryngeal cancer has a high incidence and mortality rate, especially in advanced stages. Stoma recurrence after total laryngectomy is rare but lethal, and its risk factors remain controversial. We aimed to assess whether the presence of a tracheotomy performed prior to surgical treatment for advanced laryngeal cancer represents a risk factor for recurrence of the disease in the stoma and interferes with patient survival. Methods: A retrospective study was carried out in 138 patients who underwent total laryngectomy.

pmc-13333011.title: Heart failure promotes gingival inflammation and impairs periodontal remodeling
pmc-13333011.creator: Martin Berger, Marta Rizk, Jaana-Sophia Kern, Ulrike Schulze-Späte, Sandra Hennecke, Maximilian Neuhaus, Florian Kahles, Julia Moellmann, Stefan Wolfart, Joachim Jankowski, Michael Wolf, Katharina Marx-Schütt, Nikolaus Marx
pmc-13333011.description: Observational studies suggest an association between impaired oral health and cardiovascular disease; however, the directionality and underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In particular, whether heart failure (HF) itself adversely affects oral and periodontal health has not been systematically investigated in large populations or experimental models.

pmc-13440247.title: Partnerships and practices: a scoping review of engaging older adults living with frailty in the research process
pmc-13440247.creator: Erin Davis, Ishaan Cheema, Chantelle Zimmer, Lindsay Morrison, Caitlin McClurg, Jayna Holroyd-Leduc
pmc-13440247.description: BackgroundFrailty is a multidimensional condition that increases vulnerability to poor health outcomes, yet older adults living with frailty are often underrepresented in research or involved only in limited ways. Engaging people with lived experience can improve the relevance, acceptability, and impact of research, but little is known about the involvement of older adults living with frailty across the research process.

pmc-13547458.title: Acute Effects of Exercise Snacks on Glucose and Lipid Metabolic Outcomes in Individuals with Metabolic Disorders: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-13547458.creator: Yuxin Peng, Haijun Kong, Qiang Wang, Qingyun Sun, Changxu Qu, Zhengqing Leng
pmc-13547458.description: ObjectiveTo quantify the acute effects of exercise snacks on glucose and lipid metabolism in individuals with metabolic disorders (including those with type 2 diabetes, metabolic syndrome, and overweight or obesity) compared with sedentary behavior and continuous exercise, and to examine their effects across different exercise modalities.

pmc-13640205.title: Malignancy in mirror image anatomy reveals situs inversus totalis as an anatomic modifier of oncologic care
pmc-13640205.creator: Zhongan Liu, Ganxin Wang, Kai Huang, Yan Wang, Tian Zhou, Jing Chen, Yunqing Xu, Quan Tang, Boting Yang, Jiaqin Chen, Xiangqian Yin, Sijia Zhang, Guangqin Xiao
pmc-13640205.description: BackgroundSitus inversus totalis (SIT) is a rare congenital laterality anomaly characterized by complete mirror-image transposition of the thoracic and abdominal viscera. Although SIT is not a proven cancer-predisposition syndrome, cancer in this setting challenges the spatial assumptions that guide diagnosis, staging, surgery, radiotherapy, and surveillance.

pmc-13677104.title: Factors associated with orthodontist's decision to indicated orthodontic camouflage or orthognathic surgery in skeletal class III malocclusions without growth
pmc-13677104.creator: Claudia Carranza-Buenaño, Mariano Ortiz-Pizarro, Marcos Jimmy Carruitero-Honores
pmc-13677104.description: BackgroundThe therapeutic decision depends on a complex set of factors related to both the patient and the professional.AimTo determine the factors associated with the orthodontist's decision to prescribe orthodontic camouflage or orthognathic surgery in skeletal Class III malocclusions without growth.Materials and MethodsAn online survey was conducted with 271 orthodontists.
